faqs.question: How often should I water my indoor herb garden?
faqs.answer: Most indoor herbs prefer soil that dries slightly between waterings. Check by pressing a finger about two centimetres into the soil. If it feels dry, water until a little drains from the pot, then empty the saucer. Watering needs change with light, pot size and room temperature, so rely on the soil rather than a fixed schedule.

faqs.question: Which herbs are the easiest to grow indoors for beginners?
faqs.answer: Basil, mint, chives and parsley are the easiest herbs for beginners because they adapt well to indoor containers. They sprout quickly, tolerate occasional pruning, and recover well from minor watering mistakes. Start with healthy nursery starter plants rather than seeds to see fast results on your windowsill.

faqs.question: Can culinary herbs grow indoors without direct sunlight?
faqs.answer: Most culinary herbs require bright light to thrive, but you can grow them without natural sunlight using an inexpensive LED grow light. Position the lamp about twenty centimetres above the foliage and keep it switched on for twelve to fourteen hours each day to provide enough energy for steady green growth.

faqs.question: Why are the leaves on my indoor herbs turning yellow?
faqs.answer: Yellowing leaves usually point to overwatering, poor pot drainage, or insufficient sunlight. When roots sit in soggy soil without oxygen, they cannot absorb nutrients properly. Allow the top soil layer to dry out, ensure drainage holes are clear, and move your pot to a sunnier windowsill.

faqs.question: How do I harvest indoor herbs so they keep growing?
faqs.answer: Always trim stems just above a pair of leaves using clean scissors rather than pulling leaves from the base. This encourages the plant to branch outward into two new stems. Never harvest more than one third of the foliage at once so the plant retains enough energy to recover.
